session.topic: Building a unified usage/cost tracker for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, custom)
session.current_outcome: User pivoted from a full VSCode extension (coding-agent-monitor) to a focused Node CLI (agent-tab) that wires into Claude Code's statusLine. Pivot happened via direct edits to package.json, tsconfig.json, and LICENSE.
session.project_identity_now: agent-tab (per package.json name field) — directory still named coding-agent-monitor

initial_request.verbatim_summary: Build a VSCode extension that shows how much of the limit a user has consumed across Claude Code, Codex, etc.; show daily/weekly limits + cost + tokens used; allow switching models; handle different emails per agent.
constraints_uncovered_during_q_and_a: All 6 agents in v1 (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor, custom)
Show BOTH plan usage and API token spend
Data collection: local logs + provider APIs
Multi-email: one-email-per-provider AND multiple-emails-per-provider both needed
Quality bar: 'best' — user mentioned wanting to grant to companies or create a startup

codex_cli.cost: derived; OpenAI Usage API for API-key users

copilot.tokens: no raw tokens — premium-request count only via GitHub billing API

cursor.decision: hybrid stub + experimental SQLite read with schema fingerprinting

mcp_servers.flow_a: tool-use tokens already captured in host agent's JSONL — surface as a 'by MCP server' pivot
mcp_servers.flow_b: MCP servers making their own LLM calls — registered via custom-agent manifest

what_changed.package_json: Renamed to 'agent-tab' v0.2.0. Removed all VSCode/extension/React/SQLite deps. Now a Node CLI built with plain tsc. Only deps: typescript, @types/node, vitest. Bin: agent-tab → dist/cli.js.
what_changed.tsconfig_json: Stripped to a single-project NodeNext setup (no composite, no webview-src references)
what_changed.tagline: CLI that prints today's token usage and cost across Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI. Designed to wire into Claude Code's statusLine so the active agent's tab shows above your prompt.
what_changed.scope_reduction: From 6 providers + sidebar + status bar + SQLite + graphify wiring → 3 providers (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini), CLI only, no GUI, no DB

DESIGN.md (reference for what to build later if agent-tab grows)

needs_to_be_built: src/cli.ts — entry point (Bin target is dist/cli.js)
Per-provider parsers for Claude Code / Codex / Gemini local logs
Output formats: human-readable line, JSON (for statusLine wiring), maybe ANSI-colored
README.md with installation + Claude Code statusLine wiring instructions

claude_code_statusline_integration.mechanism: Claude Code supports a statusLine config that runs a command and shows its stdout above the prompt. agent-tab should print a short, terminal-friendly line like '🟢 claude $1.20 · codex $0.03 · today'.
claude_code_statusline_integration.performance_constraint: Runs on every prompt — must be FAST (<50ms ideal, <200ms max)

open_design_questions_for_agent_tab: Output format(s)? Plain text only, or also JSON/--format=json for scripting?
Caching strategy? Re-parse every run is fine for small log volumes but expensive for users with months of data — add a small cache file?
Include cost ceiling indicators inline (e.g. '🟡 75% week')?
Should agent-tab support arguments like 'agent-tab today' / 'agent-tab week' / 'agent-tab --json'?

outstanding_open_questions_carried_over_: Any user stories missed (open in DESIGN.md §18)

rounds_with_user: Round 1: scope clarification — agents in v1, limit type, data source, multi-account
Round 3: open questions — webview framework, SQLite, Cursor, MCP
Round 4: edge case — what about Windows/Linux for iCloud-style sync
Round 5: edge cases brainstorm + agent invocation/graphify scope expansion
Round 6: locked in A + G1; went to scaffold
Round 7: user asked 'where is webview rendered, is it a browser' — clarified VSCode panel
Round 8: user pivoted package.json/tsconfig/license to agent-tab
feedback_for_future_sessions: When user says 'all agents day 1' / 'do whichever is best' / 'create a startup', they may be optimistically opening scope rather than committing to building all of it. Push back harder on scope earlier and offer a 'thin first slice' option more aggressively.
User responds well to explicit scope/effort tradeoff tables and AskUserQuestion prompts with named recommendations.
User pivots quickly when a project feels too heavy — keep the design doc as a north star but always have a shippable v0.1 inside it.
